title: “We Won’t Leave Mexico’s Mountains of Guerrero,” Governance Secretary Says
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [August 17, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/no-nos-vamos-a-salir-
de-la-montana-de-guerrero-asegura-rosa-icela-rodriguez/), an independent
Mexican investigative journalism magazine._

The federal government will maintain a permanent presence in the Upper and
Lower Mountains (Montaña Alta and Baja) of Guerrero,**a poor, largely
Indigenous highland region where fighting among organized-crime groups has
forced families to flee their homes** , with elements of the National Guard
and the Secretariat of National Defense, as well as teams from various federal
and state agencies to serve the communities affected by the displacement of
families, affirmed the Secretary of Governance, Rosa Icela Rodríguez: **" we
are not going to leave the region."**

Presenting the progress of the Master Plan for the Upper and Lower Mountains,
the official noted that, since May 13, 19 federal institutions and dozens of
agencies of the Guerrero government have worked in a coordinated manner in 19
communities of four municipalities: Atlixtac, Chilapa de Álvarez, Olinalá, and
Zapotitlán de Tablas.

She explained that the intervention was ordered by President Claudia Sheinbaum
after the displacement of families in the region became known. The order, she
said, was to serve the population **" in a close, humane, and permanent
manner,"** with people as the priority and through a strategy coordinated
among the federal, state, and municipal governments.

She detailed that the strategy was defined based on the meeting of federal
officials with the victims of the displacement; they, she said, toured the
communities and met with families, municipal and community authorities, women,
young people, senior citizens, and farmers.

From those tours, the conditions of vulnerability and insecurity were
identified and 19 priority communities were established where government
intervention is currently concentrated.

The Master Plan, as Rodríguez detailed, contemplates 13 lines of action:
peacebuilding, security, justice, agriculture, environment, health, culture,
welfare, education, infrastructure, connectivity, food, and housing. The
priority, she indicated, are girls, boys, and young people, with the goal that
they can study, train, and develop a life project in their own communities.

Likewise, she highlighted that since the start of the intervention, those
affected have been accompanied and security conditions have been strengthened
to allow their return; as a result, families from Tula and Xicotlán,
communities of Chilapa, have already returned to their homes.

She also reported that economic support was given to people whose homes were
severely affected or completely destroyed, and stressed that the return
requires guaranteeing security conditions, but also services and opportunities
to prevent new displacements and allow families to remain in their
communities.

**" We know that in order for them to be able to stay in their communities
they need security, health, education, housing, roads, food, employment
opportunities, and conditions for their daughters and sons to build their
future here,"** the official affirmed during the presentation of the Plan's
progress.

She maintained that the pacification strategy is not limited to the presence
of security forces, but includes actions to address the causes that generate
violence. In that framework, she noted that the Tianguis del Bienestar was
brought to the region, through which new essential goods were delivered free
of charge.

In the effort to pacify the area, other bodies also participated, such as the
Secretariat of Education, in charge of delivering scholarships and actions to
improve school infrastructure, while the Secretariat of Labor incorporated
young people from the region into the Youth Building the Future program and
the Secretariat of Welfare integrated people who do not yet receive any social
program.

Actions aimed at women were also reinforced to prevent and address the
violence they face, as well as to expand their autonomy and access to
protection mechanisms. In terms of health, medical services and medicines were
brought to communities that have historically had difficulties accessing these
services.

For the rural sector, the federal government launched training and technical
assistance actions, in addition to the delivery of corn and programs aimed at
improving the productivity and marketing of products, for which the
Secretariat of Agriculture is expected to join in a few days.

Rosa Icela Rodríguez noted that this visit will aim to tour the communities
and fulfill the commitment made to the population to deliver corn and beans
for food. In addition, she affirmed that actions to strengthen productive
activities and improve the economic conditions of families will continue.

In terms of security, the Secretary of State reported that a permanent command
post was established in Chilapa, with daily participation of the Secretariat
of Governance, the Secretariat of National Defense, the National Guard, the
Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection, and the Guerrero government.

She assured that the Mexican government will not withdraw its presence from
the region. **" To tell the families of the Mountains that we are not going to
leave the region, that the teams will be there permanently, as well as the
elements of the National Guard and the Secretariat of National Defense, hand
in hand with the State Police."**

She added that the institutional presence will be maintained **" for as long
as necessary"** and that the progress of the Master Plan will be reported
periodically to the communities.

The federal official stated that building peace in Guerrero requires combining
security with attention to the causes of violence.

> We, the good ones, are more than those who resort to violence; together we
> can build peace in any territory.
>
> Rosa Icela Rodríguez

Finally, she announced that this year artisanal roads will be completed and
access to the communities will be improved. She assured that social,
productive, and security programs will continue in order to recover the
conditions of well-being, security, and tranquility of the families of the
Mountains of Guerrero.
